newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Canberra to drop plans to cap fuel rebate - paper.
newsitem.headline: Canberra to drop plans to cap fuel rebate - paper.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard is expected to drop plans to cap the government's diesel fuel rebate scheme for the mining industry, The Australian Financial Review newspaper reported on Friday.
The newspaper said Howard would announce the move when he visits the Western Australia gold-mining centre of Kalgoorlie on Monday.

"The announcement that the diesel fuel rebate will not be capped will also be an important fence-mending gesture to the wider mining industry, which has had strained relations with the government over the past year," the newspaper said.
The scheme provides a tax rebate to farmers and miners for diesel fuel for off-road use.
Payouts to miners blew out to an estimated A$823.4 million in 1996/97 from an original budget projection of A$749.8 million and is forecast at A$812.9 million in the fiscal year from July.

"The government is now understood to have accepted that the estimated A$813 million cost of the diesel fuel rebate for miners in the 1997/98 budget will not be exceeded and that there is no need to impose a cap on payments," the newspaper said.
